voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: It looked like any other bill. A due date. An amount due: one hundred eighty dollars. A line that read, Yearly Web Hosting.
It went mostly to small businesses that already had a website. Their sites were hosted by someone else. The company on the bill had never hosted them.

Between twenty fifteen and twenty twenty-two, Robert Lederhilger, of Bradenton, Florida, mailed, and caused others to mail, nearly three million of them. Under names like Web Host Agents. Main Street Web Pros. Simple Domain Host.
Some of them said, in the fine print, that they were a solicitation. Not a bill. Tens of thousands of businesses paid, believing they owed it.
They got no hosting. No service of any kind. Only another invoice, a year later, asking for more.

A jury convicted him of mail fraud. In March twenty twenty-six, he was sentenced to seventy-three months. Prosecutors put the losses at nearly nine million dollars. The only product was the paper: a bill with every hallmark of one already owed.
